the_plan_in_three_lines: Nominate twice on the App Store: Family plans with the New Year Reset Challenge (submit by 2026-12-15) and Spring Produce Season (submit by 2027-02-08, or by 2026-12-01 for wider consideration).
Run three in-app events (Holiday Baking, New Year Reset, Spring Produce); the Black Friday sale and shared grocery lists are not events, so they become promotional text changes.
Google Play promotional content is not open to Tinroot on current evidence, so Play gets short description refreshes timed to the same moments.

demand_by_month.basis: sum of monthly Google searches, US, last 12 months; index = month / 12-month average

play_gate.why: Tinroot is an app, not a game. Non-game apps get promotional content only when they meet Google's premium growth tools thresholds and are in a supported category. The listing shows 500,000+ installs, under 1,000,000, so the active-user route (1.6M+ active installs) is out; only the Play spend route is left, and the user has not seen a Promotional content page in Play Console.
play_gate.check: Open Grow users > Promotional content in Play Console. If the page lets you create content, rerun this plan with Play events on.
play_gate.what_the_plan_uses_instead: store listing refreshes on Google Play

featuring_nominations.description: Family plans arrive in Tinroot on 2027-01-05: one meal plan and one grocery list shared by a household of up to 6, with each person's dislikes left out of suggestions. The same day we start the New Year Reset Challenge (an In-App Event, 2027-01-05 to 2027-01-31), which asks households to cook at home four nights a week through January. January is the busiest month of the year for meal-planning searches in the US (index 1.32 against a yearly average of 1.00). None of the three leading meal-planner listings we read on 2026-11-02 mentions a shared household plan. Priority: our most important release this winter.
featuring_nominations.supplemental_materials: up to 5 links the user supplies: press kit, artwork, TestFlight public link

past_events.verdict: confounded: Apple Ads daily budget raised 60% (user-reported) on 2026-08-31, inside the window; the lift is not the event's alone

past_events.baseline_note: the 28 days before publish overlap Lunchbox Week (to 2026-09-13); only the 14 clean days are used

past_events_method: baseline = clean days among the 28 before publish (no other event window), at least 14; z = (event mean - baseline mean) / (baseline sd x sqrt(1/n_base + 1/n_event)); clear lift when z >= 2; confounded when a paid spend change of 25% or more (up or down) is dated after the first baseline day used and on or before the event end

past_events_as_reference.measured: 12.3% more first-time downloads a day from publish to end, about 2128 extra (z 7.9)
past_events_as_reference.use: a reference, not a forecast: same badge, different season
keep expectations modest for a recipe-collection event in a below-average month
